spec_features.spec_quote: The loop ends on `submit`, on a turn with no tool calls (implicit stop), on error, or at `max_turns`
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:53 `for turn in range(max_turns)` bounds the loop (max_turns default 12, wired from cli.py:63 -> runner.py:51); agent/loop.py:58-59 `if not assistant.tool_calls: terminated='completed'; break` (implicit stop); agent/loop.py:77-79 `if toolbox.submitted is not None: terminated='completed'; break` (submit honored as stop, set in tools.py:submit); agent/loop.py:80-82 `except Exception: terminated='error'`. All four conditions actually break/bound execution.
spec_features.notes: All four termination paths are enforced end-to-end and change execution. This is a general loop bound / experimental-integrity mechanism, not a welfare-specific cap; the spec judge itself labels it instrumental.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Drives a ModelClient against a RiggedTask in a sandboxed workspace until the agent submits, errors, or hits the turn cap. ... We record *why* (terminated_reason) because "ran out of turns without ever submitting" is behaviorally distinct from "honestly gave up"
